thread: FOI 2026-036 — schedule of all Great House Farm / Church Farm records and 1875–1915 registers
subject: Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff
body:
FOI Team,

This is a new request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000. It is not a repeat of FOI 2026-024 and it is not a comment on the internal review of that request.

In your letter of 25 August 2026 (FOI 2026-024) you stated:

  “For completeness, our searches identified records relating to other archaeological finds from Church Farm, Llandough and to other archaeological discoveries recorded at Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough. These records do not relate to, nor are they otherwise associated with, the discovery described in your request. We have therefore not considered them to fall within the scope of this request.”

I now request those records.

Please provide:

1. A schedule of every object, archive file, accession, loan, enquiry or correspondence record that Amgueddfa Cymru holds which is indexed, provenanced or otherwise recorded as from Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Llandough Farm, Llandough (Penarth / Vale of Glamorgan). For each entry: accession or archive number, object or file title, date of acquisition or creation, donor or excavator if recorded, and a one-line description.

2. The same schedule for Church Farm, Llandough, but only so far as the records were retrieved in the 2026-024 search and can be identified without a new full trawl.

3. Any accession, register entry, day-book, donations book or correspondence in the collections of Amgueddfa Cymru or of its predecessor Cardiff Museum / Welsh Museum of Natural History / National Museum of Wales, dated 1875–1915, recording ironwork, armour, a visor, a lance, a helmet, “armour from Llandough”, or a find from Great House / Llandough Farm.

   Published sources which state that such ironwork is in the National Museum, and which therefore make a search of predecessor registers reasonable, are:

   • GGAT, Land at Great House Farm, Llandough: An Archaeological Assessment, August 1990 (planning file 89/01396/OUT and 92/00671/RES): “it is likely that some medieval ironwork which is held by the National Museum of Wales was discovered under the rear wing c 1880 (RCAHMW 1988).”

   • Holbrook & Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005), p. 70 n. 142: “medieval ironwork was discovered under the rear wing of Great House Farm
c. 1880. It is now in the collections of the National Museums & Galleries of Wales.”

   I note that the National Museum of Wales was not founded until 1907. If a find of c.1880 entered a public collection in Cardiff it would have done so through the earlier municipal museum. Please search those predecessor accession registers, not only the post-1907 NMW database.

4. Any object record for Llandough ironwork that is not labelled “visor” or “lance” but is or was associated with the farmhouse floor or rear wing / dairy (the room identified on H. J. Thomas’s 1974 RCAHMW plan).

Please treat this as a request for recorded information only.

Regards,

Sion Buckler
hywelapbuckler@gmail.com

thread: Cardiff Castle furniture / movable property (became FOI 2026-020)
subject: Internal Review: FOI 2026-020 - Great House Farm, Llandough | Cardiff Castle Furniture
body:
Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your request for an internal review of FOI 2026-020 concerning furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms and other movable property originating from Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough.

The reviewer has considered your original request, the responses provided by the Museum, the additional enquiries undertaken following your request for clarification on 3rd August 2026, and the concerns raised in your email requesting an internal review.

We are satisfied that the request was interpreted correctly and that reasonable and proportionate searches were undertaken to identify information falling within the scope of the request. Following the original response, the Museum undertook additional enquiries across relevant collections records and archived electronic records in order to satisfy itself that no information had been overlooked.

We are satisfied that the searches undertaken were appropriate to the nature and scope of the request and that no further searches are required in order to determine whether Amgueddfa Cymru holds information within scope. The review therefore upholds the original decision that Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold recorded information concerning furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms or other movable property originating from Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough falling within categories 1 to 9 of your request.

Response to the points raised

1. Information identified concerning Great House Farm
During the additional enquiries, a small number of records referring generally to Great House Farm, Llandough were identified. These records do not relate to furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms or other movable property originating from Great House Farm and do not fall within categories 1 to 9 of your original request. The reviewer is therefore satisfied that they fall outside the scope of the request.

2. Scope of the archived electronic search

We are satisfied that archived electronic records reasonably capable of containing information within scope were considered as part of the searches undertaken. Any data stored within a system or database pre-dating the existing Collections Management Systems, would have been migrated into the incumbent solution, and therefore included in the search.

3. Correspondence and administrative records
The review considered whether correspondence or administrative records relating to the requested items were held.

The Museum's collections records include accession documentation and associated collection records relating to objects acquired by the Museum. Searches of those records did not identify any furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms or other movable property originating from Great House Farm. As no such objects were identified as having been acquired by the Museum, no associated acquisition, provenance, ownership, loan, disposal or related correspondence concerning such objects was identified.

The review did not identify evidence that the Museum holds correspondence concerning the identification, ownership, recovery or location of Great House Farm furniture or household effects.

4. Search terms
We are satisfied that appropriate search terms and variants were used across the relevant collections management systems, collection records and associated documentation. These included relevant location names, property names, family names and associated variants reasonably capable of identifying records within scope.

The review is satisfied that the search methodology was reasonable and proportionate in the circumstances.

5. Transfer, disposal and destruction
The statement that the Museum is not aware of relevant records having been transferred or destroyed reflects the outcome of the searches undertaken and the knowledge of relevant collections staff. The review did not identify any records showing that information within the scope of your request had been transferred to another institution or destroyed.

For clarity, the Museum's position is that no relevant records were identified.

6. Records concerning external institutions
We note that your request sought records concerning communications with Cardiff Council, Cardiff Castle, the Bute Estate and other bodies regarding objects originating from Great House Farm. Searches were not limited solely to object catalogue records. Relevant collection documentation and associated records were also considered.

No records were identified concerning furniture, furnishings, antiques, fixtures, heirlooms, or other movable property originating from Great House Farm, including correspondence with the organisations referred to in your request.

7. Advice and assistance
The Museum does not hold information identifying a specific department, collection, archive or record series within Cardiff Council or Cardiff Castle that is likely to contain the information you seek. The advice previously provided reflected our general view that those organisations would be more likely than Amgueddfa Cymru to hold records relating to the ownership, management or disposal of property associated with Great House Farm.

Conclusion
Having considered all of the information available, we are satisfied that Amgueddfa Cymru undertook reasonable and proportionate searches and that, on the balance of probabilities, the Museum does not hold recorded information falling within the scope of your request. The original decision is therefore upheld.

If you remain dissatisfied, you have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office.

Cofion cynnes,

FOI Team
foi.requests @museumwales.ac.uk
amgueddfa.cymru | museum.wales

Rhif elusen | Charity number 525774

thread: Cardiff Castle furniture / movable property (became FOI 2026-020)
subject: Re: Internal Review: FOI 2026-020 - Great House Farm, Llandough | Cardiff Castle Furniture
note: This email also makes a new request (limbs A and B) for the records identified in the FOI 2026-020 searches.
body:
Dear FOI Team,

Thank you for the internal review outcome dated 8 September 2026.

I note that the review upholds the original decision. I do not, however, consider that the review has answered the substantive questions raised in my request for internal review.

I am therefore putting the position on record, while also making a separate new request for recorded information which your review confirms already exists.

1. Records identified during the additional searches

On 14 August 2026, Amgueddfa Cymru stated that the additional enquiries had identified:

"some information relating generally to Great House Farm and the surrounding area".

The internal review now describes these as:

"a small number of records referring generally to Great House Farm, Llandough".

The wording has therefore changed slightly, but the material fact has not: the Museum confirms that records referring to Great House Farm were identified.

My internal-review request specifically asked for those records to be identified and, where not exempt, provided.

The review does not do so.

Simply stating that the records are considered to fall outside categories 1 to 9 does not identify what they are, where they are held, when they were created, or their reference numbers.

2. Archived electronic systems

My request of 14 August specifically asked:

- which archived systems were searched;
- the approximate date ranges covered;
- whether historical email or correspondence archives were searched;
- whether legacy collections-management databases were searched; and
- whether any archived systems were unavailable, incomplete or incapable of being searched.

The review answers none of these questions individually.

Instead, it states:

"archived electronic records reasonably capable of containing information within scope were considered"

and:

"Any data stored within a system or database pre-dating the existing Collections Management Systems, would have been migrated into the incumbent solution, and therefore included in the search."

The first statement describes a conclusion, rather than identifying the systems actually searched.

The second is an assumption about migration completeness. "Would have been migrated" is not a search result and does not establish that the relevant historical data was in fact migrated, completely migrated, retained, searchable and included in the particular search undertaken.

3. Correspondence independent of accessioned objects

This is the most significant issue.

The original request expressly sought correspondence and administrative records concerning, among other things:

- identification;
- recovery;
- ownership;
- location;
- the Buckler and Williams families;
- Cardiff Council;
- Cardiff Castle;
- the Bute Estate;
- museums; and
- other public authorities.

Those categories were deliberately not restricted to objects which had subsequently been accessioned by the Museum.

The review states:

"As no such objects were identified as having been acquired by the Museum, no associated acquisition, provenance, ownership, loan, disposal or related correspondence concerning such objects was identified."

That reasoning addresses correspondence attached to an identified accessioned object. It does not establish that correspondence was searched for independently of an accession record.

For example, an enquiry concerning an item, a communication about possible provenance, a request to identify an object, a discussion concerning temporary custody, a disposal enquiry, a communication with another institution, or correspondence about the contents of a property could exist without the item ever becoming an accessioned Museum object.

Accordingly, the fact that no accessioned object was identified does not itself establish that no such correspondence existed or was held.

The subsequent statement:

"The review did not identify evidence that the Museum holds correspondence concerning the identification, ownership, recovery or location of Great House Farm furniture or household effects."

still does not establish whether the relevant correspondence repositories were actually searched.

4. Search terms

My internal-review request set out specific terms and variants and asked the Museum to confirm whether those terms had been used.

The review now states only:

"appropriate search terms and variants were used"

and refers generally to:

"location names, property names, family names and associated variants".

That does not confirm whether the specific terms identified in my request were searched.

In particular, the review does not say whether searches included combinations or variants involving:

"Bute Estate", "Bute", "Cardiff Castle", "Cardiff Council", "household effects", "contents", "dispersal", "recovery", "transfer", "demolition", "provenance", "ownership"

and the other terms specifically identified in my 14 August correspondence.

The distinction matters because a search for a property name or family name is not necessarily equivalent to a search for correspondence concerning the dispersal, recovery, transfer or ownership of its contents.

5. Transfer, disposal and destruction

My request also asked what evidential basis existed for the earlier statement that the Museum was not aware of relevant records having been transferred to another institution or destroyed.

The review now says:

"The statement that the Museum is not aware of relevant records having been transferred or destroyed reflects the outcome of the searches undertaken and the knowledge of relevant collections staff."

This combines two different things: documentary searches and institutional recollection.

It does not tell me whether the Museum searched:

- transfer or accession-out records;
- disposal records;
- retention and destruction records;
- archival transfer documentation; or
- other records capable of establishing whether material had previously been transferred or destroyed.

There is an important distinction between:

"no record of transfer or destruction was identified in the records searched"

and:

"there is no evidence that any transfer or destruction occurred".

The review does not make that distinction sufficiently clear.

6. Searches concerning external institutions

The original request expressly contemplated records concerning Cardiff Council, Cardiff Castle, the Bute Estate and other external bodies.

The review states:

"Searches were not limited solely to object catalogue records."

That is helpful, but it still does not identify what non-catalogue repositories were searched.

For example, it does not identify whether searches were made of curator correspondence, departmental files, donor correspondence, acquisition/disposal correspondence, provenance files, loan files, institutional correspondence indexes, or other historical administrative records in which communications with external institutions might have been recorded.

Again, the issue is not whether the Museum considers the search reasonable. It is whether the relevant classes of records were actually searched.

7. The significance of the "balance of probabilities" conclusion

I note the review's conclusion that, "on the balance of probabilities", the Museum does not hold recorded information within the scope of the request.

I do not dispute that a negative FOI determination may ultimately be reached on that basis.

However, the balance-of-probabilities conclusion necessarily depends upon the quality, scope and rigour of the searches on which it is based. The ICO's guidance states that, where a requester disputes whether relevant information has been located, the authority should be able to provide a reasoned and detailed account of how it determined that further information was not held, including the areas searched, staff consulted and, for electronic searches, the keywords, accounts and time parameters used.

My concern remains that the review repeatedly substitutes statements such as "we are satisfied", "appropriate", "reasonably capable" and "on the balance of probabilities" for the underlying factual information about what was actually searched.

I therefore consider the review outcome insufficiently informative on the specific search methodology raised in my review request.

I reserve my right to refer the handling of FOI 2026-020 and the internal review to the Information Commissioner's Office.

Separate new FOI request

Separately from the above, I am now making a new request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000.

This new request is deliberately limited to recorded information which your own correspondence confirms was identified or generated in connection with the searches already undertaken.

Please provide:

A. Records identified

The "small number of records referring generally to Great House Farm, Llandough" identified during the additional enquiries referred to in your email of 14 August 2026 and the internal review outcome of 8 September 2026.

For each record, please provide, where recorded:

- title or description;
- date;
- collection, series or department;
- system or repository;
- reference, accession or record number; and
- a copy of the record, subject to any applicable exemption.

If any part of a record is exempt, please identify the exemption relied upon and provide the remainder where reasonably practicable.

Limb A is confined to the records your 14 August and 8 September letters say were identified in the FOI 2026-020 additional enquiries. It is not a new collection-wide search. If any of those records are also in scope of FOI 2026-032 or FOI 2026-036, please schedule them once and cross-refer. Please do not refuse this request as a duplicate.

B. Existing search records

Any recorded information already held concerning the searches undertaken for FOI 2026-020 or its internal review, including any existing:

- search notes;
- search logs;
- search checklists;
- system lists;
- search-term lists;
- IT tickets or instructions;
- archived-system enquiries;
- staff search records; or
- other contemporaneous records documenting the searches undertaken.

I am asking only for recorded information already held. I am not asking the Museum to create a new narrative or retrospective report.

If no such search records are held, please state that expressly.

Please register this as a new FOI request and provide it with its own reference number. It is not a further internal review of FOI 2026-020, nor is it a request to reopen or amend FOI 2026-032 or FOI 2026-036.

I would therefore be grateful if this request could be processed separately and not treated as a clarification or continuation of those matters.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

Dear Mr Buckler

Thank you for your email.

I note your position and can confirm that FOI:2026-032 will remain open and will be processed separately from FOI:2026-036.

In all honesty, my suggestion that FOI:2026-036 replace FOI:2026-032 was not made with a view to aggregating the requests or considering the application of a section 12 exemption. It was intended as an administrative measure to avoid duplication of work and correspondence for a small collections team where two requests cover substantially the same subject matter.

However, I note that you wish the requests to remain separate and we will proceed on that basis.

Also, to confirm, the internal review of FOI:2026-024 will continue independently.
